alert.name: warden-dev-clickstream-write-throttled
alert.summary: Write provisioned throughput exceeded on the clickstream stream above 1000 per minute

logs: ALARM AWS/Kinesis/WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded StreamName=warden-dev-clickstream stat=Sum period=60s threshold GreaterThanThreshold 1000.0 datapoints=3/3 missing=notBreaching state=ALARM
STATE kinesis_stream warden-dev-clickstream StreamStatus=ACTIVE StreamMode=PROVISIONED OpenShardCount=2 RetentionPeriodHours=24 ConsumerCount=0 EncryptionType=KMS
CHANGE none on warden-dev-clickstream in the 6 h before the alert
context.alert_text: Write provisioned throughput exceeded on the clickstream stream above 1000 per minute

root_cause.hypothesis: Write traffic to the warden-dev-clickstream Kinesis stream (2 provisioned shards) exceeds the stream's write capacity, causing WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded and throttled/failed PutRecords calls. No configuration change occurred in the prior 6h, so this is a capacity/traffic mismatch rather than a misconfiguration or deploy regression.
evidence: C1 shows the WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded alarm firing 3/3 periods above threshold
C2 shows only 2 open shards (PROVISIONED mode), which caps write throughput at 2MB/s and 2000 records/s
M1 shows a very high sum of throughput-exceeded events (61240)
M3 shows ~125MB of incoming bytes in the period, consistent with exceeding 2-shard capacity
M4/M5 show matching throttled and failed PutRecords counts, confirming writes are being rejected at the shard level
C3 shows no recent change to the stream config, ruling out a recent misconfiguration or shard-count reduction as the trigger
ruled_out: Recent deploy or config change causing throttling (C3 shows none in 6h)
Consumer-side read throughput issue as root cause of write throttling (ConsumerCount=0 per C2, and read-side alarms are separate/sibling metrics)

citations.quote: none on warden-dev-clickstream in the 6 h before the alert

proposal.reasoning: The stream is provisioned with only 2 shards, and incoming write volume (bytes and throttled/failed record counts) indicates sustained traffic above the 2-shard write capacity limit (2MB/s, 2000 records/s). No recent config change explains this, pointing to organic traffic growth outpacing provisioned capacity. Increasing shard count (or switching to on-demand) directly raises the write throughput ceiling.
proposal.expected_effect: Increased shard count raises the stream's write throughput capacity, reducing or eliminating WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded errors and PutRecords throttling/failures.

reasons: none of the cited evidence bears on scale_up (it names none of: memory, oom, throttl, cpu, concurrency, pool...).
